3.
ननु विषयग्रहणेनैव स्त्रीरूपविषयस्य गृहीतत्वात्पुनरुक्तिरनर्थकेति चेन्न ।
If it be objected that since the object in the form of woman is already included within the general mention of sense-objects, this separate repetition is redundant — it is not so.
अतीतानन्तकोटिजन्मार्जितस्त्रीविषयोपभोगजनितवासनायाः तीव्रतरत्वात्, शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धमैथुनात्मकषडेन्द्रियविषयाणामेकत्रैव स्त्रीपिण्डे सम्भवात्, सर्वेभ्योऽपि विषयेभ्यः संसारार्णवनिमज्जनहेतुभूतेभ्यः स्त्रीव्यक्तेरेव प्रबलतरत्वात्सर्वानर्थमूलत्वाच्च स्त्रीरूपे विषयेऽतितरां वैरस्यं सम्पादनीयमित्यभिप्रायं द्योतयितुं पुनर्ग्रहणम् ।
Its separate mention is made in order to highlight that deep aversion must be cultivated specifically toward the woman-object, because the vāsanā accumulated from its enjoyment across countless past births is exceptionally intense, because all six sensory objects (sound, touch, form, taste, smell, and sexual union) exist combined in a woman's physical body, and because among all objects causing one to sink in the ocean of saṃsāra, attachment to woman is the strongest and the root of all ruin.
तथा चोक्तम् ।
And so it is said:
यस्य स्त्री तस्य भोगेच्छा निस्त्रीकस्य क्व भोगभूः । स्त्रियं त्यक्त्वा जगत्त्यक्तं जगत्त्यक्त्वा सूखी भवेत् ॥
He who has a woman has desire for enjoyment; for him who is without a woman, where is any scope for enjoyment? By renouncing woman, the whole world is renounced; having renounced the world, one becomes happy.
लिन्दु माभिगां लिन्दु माभिगाम् (छा. ८.१४.१) इति ।
May I not enter the slippery womb, may I not enter the slippery womb! (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 8.14.1).
सर्वेन्द्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः (क. १.१.२६) इति ।
They wear away the vigor of all the senses (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1.26).
अथ यद्यज्ञ इत्याचक्षते ब्रह्मचर्यमेव तत् (छा. ८.५.१) इत्यादिना बहुप्रपञ्चेन केवलब्रह्मचर्यस्य स्त्रीविषयपरित्यागलक्षणस्य वैराग्यस्य मैथुनासमाचारस्य दहराद्युपासनान्तरप्राप्यब्रह्मलोकावाप्तिसाधनत्वमुच्यते ।
Through extensive elaboration such as Now, what they call sacrifice is really celibacy (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 8.5.1), pure celibacy — characterized as dispassion consisting in the total abandonment of sexual intercourse and the woman-object — is declared to be the direct means of attaining Brahmaloka, which is otherwise attainable through Dahara and other higher meditations.
4.
वेदान्तश्रवणादिप्रसङ्गे सति तत्प्रतिबन्धकशीतोष्णक्षुत्पिपासादिद्वन्द्वान्तरायसहनरूपा तितिक्षा कार्या ।
When undertaking the hearing (*śravaṇa*) and contemplation of Vedānta, forbearance (*titikṣā*) in the form of enduring the obstacles of dualities such as cold, heat, hunger, and thirst that obstruct it, must be practiced.
अन्यथा क्षुत्पिपासादिप्रतीकारे व्यापृतचित्तस्य श्रवणादिप्रवृत्त्यसम्भवः स्यात् ।
Otherwise, for one whose mind is absorbed in seeking remedies for hunger, thirst, and discomfort, engagement in hearing (*śravaṇa*) and reflection would be impossible.
अतोऽवश्यं तितिक्षा सम्पादनीया ।
Therefore, *titikṣā* must certainly be acquired.
5.
आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु । बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ (क. १.३.३)
'Know the *ātman* as the master of the chariot, the body as the chariot itself, the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.3)
इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांस्तेषु गोचरान् । आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥ (क. १.३.४)
'The senses they call the horses, and the objects their paths; the self conjoined with body, senses, and mind, the wise call the enjoyer.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.4)
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान् भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ (क. १.३.५)
'He who is devoid of discrimination, always with an unrestrained mind, his senses become uncontrollable, like vicious horses of a charioteer.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.5)
यस्तु विज्ञानवान् भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ (क. १.३.६)
'He who possesses discrimination, with a disciplined mind always, his senses are obedient, like good horses of a charioteer.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.6)
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान् भवत्यमनस्कः सदाऽशुचिः । न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति ॥ (क. १.३.७)
'He who is devoid of discrimination, unmindful, and ever impure, does not reach that goal and enters transmigration.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.7)
यस्तु विज्ञानवान् भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः । स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते ॥ (क. १.३.८)
'He who possesses discrimination, with a controlled mind and ever pure, reaches that state whence he is not born again.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.8)
विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनःप्रग्रहवान् नरः । सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ (क. १.३.९)
'The man who has discrimination as his charioteer and holds the reins of the mind reaches the end of the journey — that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3.9)
शरीररूपरथस्येन्द्रियाणि हयाः, मनः प्रग्रहः, बुद्धिः सारथिः, आत्मा यजमानो रथी ।
Of the chariot in the form of the body, the sense-organs are the horses, the mind is the reins, the intellect is the charioteer, and the *ātman*, the master, is the passenger.
यस्य यजमानस्य बुद्धिरूपसारथिर्विज्ञानवान् कुशलस्तस्येन्द्रियाश्वाः सन्मार्गे गत्वा यजमानं मोक्षं गमयेयुः ।
That master whose charioteer in the form of intellect is discriminating and skilled, his horses of the senses, treading upon the righteous path, lead him to liberation.
विपरीतबुद्धिसारथ्युपेतस्तु यजमानोऽदान्तेन्द्रियाश्वैर्निषिद्धमार्गेण नरकमाप्नुयात् ।
However, the master endowed with a perverted charioteer of intellect would reach hell via the forbidden path driven by unruly horses of the senses.
तस्मान्मुमुक्षुर्बुद्धिसारथिं स्वेच्छाचारात्प्रतिनिवर्तयन् इन्द्रियाश्वान् सन्मार्गे प्रवर्तयेत् ।
Therefore, turning back the intellect-charioteer from wilful self-indulgence, the seeker of liberation should direct the sense-horses onto the righteous path.
अत्र बुद्धिसारथेः स्ववशतापादनं शमः ।
Here, bringing the intellect-charioteer under one's own control is *śama*.
इन्द्रियाश्ववशीकरणं दमः इति ।
And subjugating the horses of the senses is *dama*.
अन्यत्राप्युक्तम् — मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः । बन्धाय विषयासक्तं मुक्त्यै निर्विषयं स्मृतम् ॥ (प. ब्र. यो. ११७) चित्तं कारणमर्थानां तस्मिन् सति जगत्त्रयम् । तस्मिन् क्षीणे जगत्क्षीणं तच्चिकित्स्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥ इति ।
Elsewhere too it is stated: 'The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for men: attached to objects it leads to bondage, free from objects it is deemed to lead to liberation' (Para-brahma Yoga 117); 'The mind is the cause of all phenomena; when it exists, the three worlds exist; when it dissolves, the world dissolves; therefore it must be diligently treated.'
सारथेरश्वानां च यथा परस्पराधीनता तथा बुद्धेरिन्द्रियाणां च परस्पराधीनता वर्तते ।
Just as there is mutual dependence between the charioteer and the horses, so too there exists mutual dependence between the intellect and the senses.
विचित्रानेकमणिघटितमालाया यथा चामीकरत्वेनैकत्वव्यवहारस्तथा षण्णामपि विलक्षणानां शमादीनां परस्परापेक्षणेनैकसाधनत्वव्यवहारः ।
Just as a necklace composed of diverse variegated gems is spoken of as one unit by virtue of its golden thread, so too the six distinct virtues, *śama* and the rest, are treated as a single unified discipline due to their mutual interdependence.
शमादीनां परस्परसहायता चेत्थम् —
And the mutual assistance among *śama* and the others is as follows:
(१) मनोवशीकरणमन्तरेण इन्द्रियस्य जयो न सम्भवतीति दमः शमं अपेक्षते ।
(1) Because conquering the senses is not possible without subjugating the mind, *dama* depends upon *śama*.
(२) बहिर्मुखस्य मनसो दारपुत्रवित्ताद्यासक्तस्य वेदान्तशास्त्रगुरुप्रभृतिषु पूर्णश्रद्धासम्भवाच्छ्रद्धा शममपेक्षते ।
(2) Since complete faith in the *Vedānta* scriptures, the *guru*, etc. is impossible for an extroverted mind attached to wife, children, and wealth, *śraddhā* depends upon *śama*.
(३) अन्तरा मनोनिरोधं ब्रह्मणि चित्तैकाग्र्यासम्भवात्समाधानं शममपेक्षते ।
(3) Since one-pointedness of consciousness upon Brahman is impossible without restraining the mind, *samādhāna* depends upon *śama*.
(४) क्षीरादिना संवर्धितो मार्जारः पाशाद्यवशीकृतत्वान्मूषकदर्शनमात्रेण यथा तद्ग्रहणाय धावेदेवं विषयेभ्य उपरतमपि मनो निरोधादिभिरवशीकृतं चेत्, सम्प्राप्ते विषये प्राचीनवासनावेगाद्धावेदित्यत उपरतिः शममपेक्षते ।
(4) Just as a cat reared on milk etc., not being restrained by a leash, would pounce at the mere sight of a mouse to catch it, similarly even a mind withdrawn from objects, if not fully mastered through restraint etc., would rush forth at the presentation of an object by the impetus of past impressions (*vāsanā*); therefore *uparati* depends upon *śama*.
(५) अन्तर्मुखीभूतमनसैव शीतोष्णादिद्वन्द्वसहनं कर्तुं शक्यते, न तु बहिर्मुखीभूतमनसेत्यतस्तितिक्षापि शममपेक्षते ।
(5) Endurance of pairs of opposites such as heat and cold can only be practiced by an introverted mind, not by an extroverted one; therefore *titikṣā* also depends upon *śama*.
इति शमः दमादीनां पञ्चानां सहकारी ।
Thus *śama* is an auxiliary factor for the remaining five virtues, beginning with *dama*.
(६) विना तु इन्द्रियदमेन मनो न जीयत इत्यतः शमोऽपि दममाकाङ्क्षते ।
(6) Without sense-control, however, the mind cannot be conquered; therefore *śama* also requires *dama*.
(७) रूपरसादिविषयासक्तस्य गुरुवेदान्तवाक्यश्रद्धा न जायेतेत्यतः श्रद्धापि दममाकाङ्क्षते ।
(7) For one attached to objects of form, taste, etc., faith in the teachings of the *guru* and *Vedānta* cannot arise; therefore *śraddhā* also requires *dama*.
(८) इन्द्रियनिग्रहमन्तरा चैकाग्र्यं न मनसो जायेतेत्यतः समाधानमपि दममाकाङ्क्षते ।
(8) And without sense-restraint, one-pointedness of the mind cannot arise; therefore *samādhāna* also requires *dama*.
(९) ऋते त्विन्द्रियदमेनानुभूतविषयकवासनावेगवशात् दृष्टेष्टविषयेषु पुनः पुनरिच्छा जायेतेत्यत उपरतिरपि दममाकाङ्क्षते ॥
(9) For without sense-control, desires for seen and coveted objects would arise repeatedly under the impulse of latent impressions of previously experienced objects; therefore *uparati* also requires *dama*.
20 · मुमुक्षा नाम
स्वस्वरूपभूतब्रह्मावाप्तिरनर्थनिवृत्तिश्च मोक्ष इति तस्मिन् तीव्रतरेच्छा ।
Mokṣa is the attainment of Brahman, which is one's own true nature, and the absolute cessation of all suffering (evil); [mumukṣutva is] the intense desire for that mokṣa.
21 · ज्ञानोत्पत्तिसाधनानि
विवेकादिचतुष्टयं, श्रवणमनननिदिध्यासनानि त्रीणि, तत्त्वम्पदार्थशोधनं चेत्यष्टौ ज्ञानसाधनानि ।
The fourfold means beginning with discrimination (sādhana-catuṣṭaya), the three comprising hearing (śravaṇa), reflection (manana), and contemplation (nididhyāsana), and the ascertainment of the true meaning of the terms 'tat' and 'tvam' (padārtha-śodhana)—these eight are the means for attaining knowledge.
22 · अन्तरङ्गबहिरङ्गसाधनानि
विवेकादीनि पूर्वोक्तसाधनान्यष्टावपि अन्तरङ्गसाधनानि ।
All the eight previously mentioned means, beginning with discrimination, are proximate means (antaraṅga-sādhana).
यज्ञदानतपादीनि बहिरङ्गसाधनानि ।
Sacrifice, charity, penance, and the like are remote means (bahiraṅga-sādhana).
अनयोर्मुमुक्षुर्जिज्ञासौत्कट्येऽन्तरङ्गमेव साधनमनुतिष्ठेत् ।
Between these two, when the desire for knowledge is intense, the seeker of liberation should practise the proximate means alone.
अन्तरेण त्विन्द्रियदमेन विषयसान्निध्यवशात् क्षुभितं सन्मनः शीतोष्णादिद्वन्द्वं न विषहेतेत्यतस्तितिक्षापि दममाकाङ्क्षते ।
(10) Without sensory restraint, the mind, agitated by proximity to sense-objects, could not endure pairs of opposites like heat and cold; therefore, even forbearance requires sense-restraint.
इति दमः शमादीनां पञ्चानां सहकारी ।
Thus sense-restraint is an auxiliary to the other five beginning with calm (śama).
श्रीसद्गुरुवेदान्तशास्त्रेषु तीव्रतरश्रद्धाभावे श्रवणादौ श्रवणोपयोगिशमादिसाधने प्रवृत्तिर्न जायेतेत्यतः शमादयोऽपि श्रद्धामपेक्षन्ते ।
(11) In the absence of very intense faith in the venerable Sadguru and the Vedānta scriptures, no engagement would arise in *śravaṇa* etc. or in the means like *śama* that are helpful for hearing; therefore, *śama* and the rest also depend on faith.
अन्तरेण चित्तैकाग्र्यं शमादिसाधनानि न सिद्ध्येरन्नित्यतः शमादयः समाधानमपेक्षन्ते ।
(12) Without concentration of mind, the disciplines beginning with calm cannot be accomplished; therefore, *śama* and the rest depend on concentration (*samādhāna*).
विषयेभ्यश्चेत् स्यादनुपरतं चित्तं तदा शमादयो न सिद्ध्येरन्नित्यतः शमादय उपरतिमपेक्षन्ते ।
(13) If the mind is not withdrawn from objects, then *śama* and the rest cannot be achieved; therefore, *śama* and the rest depend on withdrawal (*uparati*).
शीतोष्णक्षुत्पिपासालाभालाभादिविचित्रविषयानुभवजनिततापत्रयासहं चेत् स्याच्चित्तम्, मनसः शमः, इन्द्रियाणां दमः, गुरुवेदान्तवाक्ये श्रद्धा, चित्तैकाग्र्यं, प्राप्तोपभोगयोग्यधनादिविषयेभ्य उपरतिश्चेत्यादिसाधनानि न सिद्ध्येरन्नित्यतः शमादयस्तितिक्षामपेक्षन्ते ।
(14) If the mind cannot endure the threefold afflictions caused by the experience of diverse objects like heat, cold, hunger, thirst, gain, and loss, then the disciplines—mental calm, sense-control, faith in the words of Guru and Vedānta, mental concentration, and withdrawal from enjoyable wealth already obtained—could not be attained; therefore, *śama* and the rest depend upon forbearance (*titikṣā*).
इत्थं परस्परसापेक्षत्वात् शमादिषट्कमपि मिलित्वैकमेव साधनमित्युच्यते ।
In this manner, due to mutual interdependence, the sixfold group beginning with *śama* is collectively considered a single means.
टिप्पणी
1.
यथा बुभुक्षितस्यानन्यचित्ततया अन्नपानादिसम्पिपादयिषा, यथाग्निना दग्धस्य तच्छान्त्यर्थं जलाशयान्वेषणम्, एवं संसारतापत्रयपरिवेष्टितस्य ततो मुमुक्षायामनन्यचित्ततया तदैकाग्र्यमेव तत्र तीव्रता ।
Just as a hungry man has an exclusive desire to obtain food and drink, or as one scorched by fire desperately searches for a body of water to relieve it, similarly, for one surrounded by the threefold miseries of *saṃsāra*, one-pointed focus with undistracted mind upon liberation is itself 'intensity' (*tīvratā*).
प्रयोजनमनुद्दिश्य न मन्दोऽपि प्रवर्तते इति न्यायेन मोक्षरूपफले मन्देच्छाभावे निष्कामकर्मानुष्ठाने न कस्यचित्प्रवृत्तिः स्यात् ।
By the maxim, 'Even a simpleton does not act without a motive,' if there were no desire whatsoever for the fruit of liberation, no one would engage in desireless action (*niṣkāma-karma*).
अतो मन्दमुमुक्षया सकलेतरसाधनेभ्यः प्रथमतो भाव्यम् ।
Therefore, a mild desire for liberation must exist prior to all other disciplines.
तदानीं सा न तीव्रा स्यात् ।
At that stage it may not be intense.
सिद्धेषु त्वितरसाधनेषु सा तीव्रा भवेत् ।
However, once the other disciplines are accomplished, it becomes intense.
सैव तीव्रेच्छा श्रवणादिप्रवृत्तौ निदानम् ।
That very intense desire is the root cause for engaging in *śravaṇa* and the rest.
2.
यथा हंसेन क्षीरनीरविवेचनं क्रियते, यथा वा दध्नो नवनीतस्य विवेचनं क्रियते एवं चिज्जडयोरुपलभ्यमानकारणकार्यत्वाधिष्ठानारोपितत्त्व-दृग्दृश्यत्व-साक्षिसाक्ष्यत्वादिस्वरूपस्य शास्त्रानुसारिविचारणमेव शोधनम् ।
Just as a swan separates milk from water, or as butter is separated from curd, similarly, the scriptural inquiry into the nature of consciousness (*cit*) and the inert (*jaḍa*)—perceived as cause-and-effect, substratum-and-superimposition, seer-and-seen, witness-and-witnessed, etc.—is alone termed ascertainment (*śodhana*).
3.
धनुषि लक्ष्यवेधाय सन्धीकृतो वा, धनुषो मुक्तो वा बाणो यथा तद्वेधनेऽन्तरङ्गसाधनं भवति, एवं ज्ञानोत्पत्तौ विवेकादयोऽष्टावप्यन्तरङ्गसाधनानि सन्निपत्योपकारकत्वात् ।
Just as an arrow fitted to the bow or released from it is the proximate instrument in piercing the target, so too all eight disciplines beginning with discrimination are proximate means for the rise of knowledge because they aid it directly (*sannipatyopakārakatvāt*).
4.
यथा धनुः लक्ष्यवेधने बहिष्ठमेव सत् बाणसन्धानद्वारोपकारकत्वाद्बहिरङ्गसाधनम् ।
Just as the bow is an external, remote means in piercing the target since it assists mediately through the aiming of the arrow.
यस्य साधनस्य श्रवणादिकं तत्कार्यभूतमपरोक्षज्ञानं वा दृष्टं फलं, तदन्तरङ्गमित्युच्यते ।
That discipline whose visible fruit is *śravaṇa* etc., or direct realization born of it, is termed an *antaraṅga* (proximate) means.
विवेकादिचतुष्टयं श्रवणे मुख्यसाधनम्; बहिर्विषयाभिमुखस्य विवेकाद्ययोगाच्छ्रवणाद्यसिद्धेः ।
The fourfold discipline beginning with discrimination is the principal means for *śravaṇa*, because for one oriented towards external objects, lacking discrimination etc., *śravaṇa* and the rest cannot be achieved.
एवं श्रवणमनननिदिध्यासनान्यपि ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कारे मुख्यसाधनानि, तदभावे तदभावात् ।
Likewise, hearing (*śravaṇa*), reflection (*manana*), and contemplation (*nididhyāsana*) are the principal means for Brahman-realization, because in their absence, realization cannot take place.
तत्त्वमोः पदार्थज्ञानमप्यखण्डमहावाक्यार्थाभेदज्ञाने कारणम् ।
Knowledge of the meaning of the terms 'Tat' and 'Tvam' is also the cause for knowing the non-dual identity signified by the impartite *mahāvākya*.
इत्थं विवेकादिचतुष्टयस्य श्रवणादौ, श्रवणादेश्चापरोक्षज्ञाने तत्त्वम्पदार्थज्ञानस्य महावाक्यार्थज्ञाने च क्रमेण कारणभावापत्तौ पूर्वोक्तान्यष्टावप्यन्तरङ्गसाधनानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
Thus, since the fourfold means is the cause of *śravaṇa* etc., *śravaṇa* etc. is the cause of direct realization, and knowledge of the word-meanings of 'Tat' and 'Tvam' is the cause of understanding the *mahāvākya*, all the previously stated eight are called proximate means.
अतस्तानि साधनानि मुमुक्षुणा तीव्रतरश्रद्धया सम्पादनीयानि ।
Therefore, these disciplines must be cultivated by the seeker of liberation with very intense faith.
यस्य साधनस्य श्रवणं वा ज्ञानं वा दृष्टप्रयोजनं न भवति, किन्तु चित्तशुद्धिमात्रं फलं, तत् ज्ञानस्य बहिरङ्गसाधनम् ।
That discipline whose visible purpose is neither *śravaṇa* nor knowledge, but whose result is mere purification of the mind, is a remote means (*bahiraṅga-sādhana*) to knowledge.
एवं यज्ञादिकर्माणि बहिरङ्गसाधनानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
Thus actions like sacrifice etc. are called remote means.
यद्यपि तानि सकामस्यानुष्ठीयमानानि संसारहेतुत्वेन बन्धाय भवन्ति न तु चित्तशुद्धये, तथापि यथाक्रतु-श्रुत्या संयोगपृथक्त्वन्यायेन च निष्कामस्य चित्तशुद्धये भवन्ति ।
Although, when performed by one who harbors desire, they lead to bondage as causes of *saṃsāra* and not to mental purification, nevertheless, according to the *'yathā-kratu'* Śruti and by the principle of distinct application (*saṃyoga-pṛthaktva-nyāya*), they serve to purify the mind of a desireless aspirant.
तस्मान्निष्कामस्य मुमुक्षोः चित्तशुद्धिद्वारा ज्ञानोत्पत्तिहेतुत्वाद्यज्ञादीनि बहिरङ्गसाधनानि, विवेकादीनि त्वन्तरङ्गसाधनानि इति चोच्यन्ते ।
Therefore, for the desireless seeker, because they cause the rise of knowledge mediately through purification of the mind, sacrifice and the rest are termed remote means, while discrimination etc. are termed proximate means.
बहिरङ्गानि = विप्रकृष्टानि ।
'Remote means' (*bahiraṅgāni*) = distant / indirect means.
अन्तरङ्गानि = सन्निकृष्टानि ।
'Proximate means' (*antaraṅgāni*) = direct / close means.
यज्ञादिनिखिलकर्माणि तत्साधनवित्तदारपुत्रादीनि च निश्शेषं यः सन्न्यस्यति स एव ज्ञाने उत्तमाधिकारी ।
He who completely renounces all rituals like sacrifices along with their means—wealth, wife, sons, etc.—is alone the highest eligible aspirant (*uttamādhikārī*) for knowledge.
ज्ञानाधिकारिणि यज्ञादीनामसम्भवात्तानि बहिरङ्गानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
Because sacrifices and such rituals are impossible in one who is already qualified for knowledge, they are termed remote means (*bahiraṅga*).
23 · विवेकादीनामन्तरङ्गसाधनत्वनिरूपणं
विवेकादीनां ज्ञानाधिकारिणि सम्भवात् तानि अन्तरङ्गानि इति उच्यन्ते ।
Because discrimination and the other aids exist within the person qualified for knowledge, they are called proximate (internal) means.
एवं नित्य-नैमित्तिक-यज्ञादीनि श्रौत-स्मार्त-कर्माणि, सगुण-उपासनादीनि च मल-विक्षेपादि-दोष-निराकरणेन चित्त-शुद्धिम् ऐकाग्र्यं च उत्पाद्य जिज्ञासोत्पत्ति-द्वारा ज्ञाने आराद्-उपकारकत्वाद् बहिरङ्गानि इति उच्यन्ते ।
Thus, the obligatory and occasional Vedic and Smṛti rituals, as well as meditations on the qualified deity, are called remote (external) means because, by eliminating the faults of impurity and distraction, they produce mental purity and single-pointed focus, thereby remotely aiding knowledge through generating the desire to know (*jijñāsā*).
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥ (भ. गी. ६.३) इत्यादिवचनैः अन्तरङ्ग-साधन-सिद्ध्यनन्तरम् एव बहिरङ्ग-साधनानि परित्याज्यानि ।
In accordance with passages like: For a sage seeking to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means; for that same sage who has attained yoga, quiescence (renunciation) is said to be the means (भ. गी. ६.३), external means are to be abandoned only after the proximate internal means have been accomplished.
अन्यथा विवेकादि-साधन-सिद्धेः पूर्वम् एव नित्य-नैमित्तिक-यज्ञादि-कर्म-परित्यागे उभय-भ्रष्टः अधः पतेद् एव ।
Otherwise, if one abandons obligatory and occasional sacrifices prior to the attainment of discrimination and other inner aids, one will certainly fall down, ruined from both paths.
यथा अन्धकूपे पतितो दुर्बलं तृणाद्याश्रयमवलम्ब्य लम्बमानः स्वोद्धरणाय प्रहितदृढतररज्ज्ववलम्बनात् पूर्वम् एव प्राक्तनावलम्बं परित्यजन् अधः पतेत् तद्वत् ।
Just as a man who has fallen into a blind well, hanging on by clinging to a frail clump of grass, would fall to the bottom if he let go of his former hold before catching the stronger rope lowered for his rescue — even so is this case.
अत्र च अयं विशेषः - विवेकादीनां श्रवणे उपयुक्तत्वात् श्रवणादीनां च ज्ञाने विनियुक्तत्वात् विवेकादीनि अपेक्ष्य श्रवणादीनि अन्तरङ्ग-साधनानि ।
And here lies this distinction: because discrimination and the rest are useful for *śravaṇa* (hearing the texts), while *śravaṇa* and the rest are directly engaged in producing knowledge, *śravaṇa*, etc., are proximate internal means relative to discrimination, etc.
विवेकादीनि तु तदपेक्षया बहिरङ्गानि ।
Discrimination and the rest, however, are external in comparison to them (*śravaṇa*, etc.).
यद्यपि सर्वत्र वेदान्तशास्त्रेषु ज्ञानं प्रति विवेकादीनि अन्तरङ्ग-साधनत्वेन एव उक्तानि न बहिरङ्ग-साधनत्वेन, तथापि विवेकादीनां हि, ज्ञाने अन्तरङ्ग-साधनीभूत-श्रवणम् एव प्रत्यक्षं फलम् ।
Although in all Vedānta treatises discrimination, etc., are explicitly stated to be proximate means towards knowledge and not external means, nevertheless, *śravaṇa* (which is the direct internal means to knowledge) is the immediate fruit of discrimination and the other qualifications.
श्रवणादिवद् विवेकादीन्यपि जिज्ञासुना मुमुक्षुणा अवश्यम् आदर्तव्यान्येव, न तु यज्ञादिवद् हातव्यानि ।
Just like *śravaṇa* and the rest, discrimination and the other aids must necessarily be cultivated by the seeker of liberation; they are not to be abandoned like sacrifices and rituals.
तस्मात् कारणात्, यज्ञाद्यपेक्षया अन्तरङ्गत्वात् च तानि अन्तरङ्ग-साधनानि इति उच्यन्ते ।
For that reason, and because they are more proximate compared to sacrifices and other rituals, they are termed proximate (internal) means.
(A. 24-26) ज्ञाने मुख्य-अन्तरङ्ग-साधन-श्रवणादीनां लक्षणम् -
(Avartas 24-26) The definitions of *śravaṇa* and the other primary internal means for knowledge:
लक्षणम्ज्ञाने मुख्यान्तरङ्गसाधनश्रवणादीनां लक्षणम्॥ २४–२६ ॥
24 · श्रवणलक्षणं
वस्तुतो विचार्यमाणे श्रवणादीन्यपि नान्तरङ्गसाधनानि ज्ञानस्य, किन्तु तत्त्वमस्यादिमहावाक्यान्येव; प्रमाणफलत्वात् ज्ञानस्य ।
In reality, when investigated, even *śravaṇa* and the rest are not the direct means to knowledge, but rather the *mahāvākya*s such as 'Tat Tvam Asi' alone; because knowledge is the fruit of an instrument of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*).
तं त्वौपनिषदं पुरुषम्(बृ. ३.९.२६) वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः (मु. ३.२.६) इत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः ।
This is known from Śruti passages such as: 'I ask you about that Puruṣa revealed only in the Upaniṣads' (Bṛ. 3.9.26) and 'Those who have well ascertained the meaning through the knowledge of Vedānta' (Mu. 3.2.6).
श्रवणं नाम युक्त्या षड्विधतात्पर्यलिङ्गैः वेदान्तवाक्यानामद्वितीये प्रत्यगभिन्नब्रह्मणि तात्पर्यनिर्णयानुकूलचेतोवृत्तिविशेषः ।1,2
*Śravaṇa* is indeed that particular mental modification (*vṛtti*) conducive to determining the purport of the Vedāntic statements as resting in the non-dual Brahman non-different from the inner self, through reasoning by means of the sixfold indicators of intention (*ṣaḍvidha-tātparya-liṅga*).
टिप्पणी
1.
वेदान्तश्रवणं हि दीर्घकालं नैरन्तर्येणादरेणानुष्ठेयम् ।
Hearing (*śravaṇa*) of Vedānta must indeed be practiced for a long time, without interruption, and with reverence.
विवेकादिसाधनचतुष्टयरहितस्य बहिर्मुखस्य निरन्तरायतया श्रवणं न सिद्ध्येत् ।
For one who is extroverted and devoid of the fourfold qualifications beginning with discrimination (*viveka*), *śravaṇa* cannot be accomplished without obstacle.
श्रवणमन्तरा मनननिदिध्यासने न स्याताम् ।
Without *śravaṇa*, reflection (*manana*) and meditation (*nididhyāsana*) cannot take place.
अतः श्रवणाद्यङ्गतया विवेकादिचतुष्टयमवश्यं सम्पाद्य विचारयेत् ।
Therefore, having necessarily acquired the fourfold qualifications beginning with *viveka* as auxiliaries to *śravaṇa* and the rest, one should inquire.
लोके शास्त्रज्ञोऽपि विवेकमात्रयुक्तोऽप्यत्यन्तविषयासक्तः सन् काम्यकर्मसु प्रवर्तते ।
In the world, even a scholar of scriptures endowed with mere intellectual discrimination may engage in desire-prompted actions if deeply attached to sense objects.
अतो द्वितीयसाधनेनेहामुत्रफलभोगवैराग्येणाप्यवश्यं भाव्यम् ।
Therefore, one must necessarily possess the second means as well, which is dispassion (*vairāgya*) toward the enjoyment of fruits here and in the hereafter.
प्रथमद्वितीयाभ्यां सम्पन्नोऽपि कश्चित्कोपादिना तप्यत इति तृतीयेनापि शमादिसाधनेन भाव्यम् ।
Though endowed with the first two, one may still be tormented by anger and such passions; therefore, one must also possess the third means, namely the group of virtues beginning with *śama*.
सत्स्वपि त्रिषु साधनेषु मुमुक्षाभावे श्रवणादौ न प्रवर्तेतेति चतुर्थ्या अपि मुमुक्षया अवश्यं भाव्यं इति ।
Even when the three means are present, if desire for liberation (*mumukṣā*) is absent, one would not engage in *śravaṇa* and the rest; therefore, one must necessarily possess the fourth, namely *mumukṣā*.
2.
धूमज्ञानेन वह्निज्ञानस्य जायमानत्वाद्यथा धूमो वह्निनिश्चये लिङ्गं, तथाद्वैतस्वरूपे प्रत्यगभिन्नब्रह्मणि वेदान्तानां तात्पर्यमिति, उपक्रमोपसंहारादिषड्विधतात्पर्यलिङ्गैर्निर्णीयमानत्वात्तानि तात्पर्यलिङ्गानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
Just as smoke is an indicator (*liṅga*) in determining fire because fire-knowledge arises from smoke-knowledge, likewise, because the purport of the Upaniṣads as resting in Brahman non-different from the inner self (of non-dual nature) is determined by the sixfold indicators beginning with *upakrama* and *upasaṃhāra*, they are called the indicators of purport (*tātparya-liṅga*).
युक्तिशब्देन चैतानि लिङ्गानि गृह्यन्ते ।
And by the word 'reasoning' (*yukti*), these very indicators are meant.
तानि च लिङ्गानि षड्विधानिउपक्रमोपसंहारावभ्यासोऽपूर्वताफलम् । अर्थवादोपपत्ती च लिङ्गं तात्पर्यनिर्णये ॥ इति वचनात् ।
And those indicators are of six kinds, according to the verse: 'The initial statement and the conclusion, repetition, novelty, fruit, eulogy, and logical reasoning are the indicators in determining the purport.'
(१) छान्दोग्ये षष्ठप्रपाठके सदेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदेकमेवाद्वितीयम् (छा. ६-२-१) इति प्रकरणोपक्रमे योऽर्थ उक्तः स एवोपसंहारेऽपि ऐतदात्म्यमिदं सर्वं तत्सत्यं स आत्मा(छा. ६.१६.३) इत्युपसंहृतः ।
(1) In the sixth chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad, the meaning that was stated at the beginning of the section: 'In the beginning, my dear, this was Existence alone, one only without a second' (Chā. 6.2.1), is concluded in the very same manner at the end: 'All this has this as its Self; that is the Truth; that is the Self' (Chā. 6.16.3).
इत्युपक्रमोपसंहारैकरूप्यमेकं लिङ्गम् ।
Thus, the harmony (*aikarūpya*) between the beginning and the conclusion is the first indicator.
(२) यथा अर्थी पुरुषः स्वाभिलषितमर्थं भिन्नभिन्नवाक्यैः पुनः पुनः प्रकटीकुर्यादेवं भिन्नभिन्नयुक्तिमद्वचनैः प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मैक्यं तत्त्वमसि(छा. ६.८.७) इति नवकृत्वः पुनः पुनरभ्यस्यते ।
(2) Just as a desirous person expresses his desired matter again and again using different sentences, similarly the identity of the inner self and Brahman is repeated nine times by means of statements endowed with various reasons: 'That thou art' (Chā. 6.8.7).
इत्यभ्यासोऽपि द्वितीयं लिङ्गम् ॥
Thus, repetition (*abhyāsa*) is also the second indicator.
25 · मननलक्षणं
मननं नाम प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मैक्यसाधक-तद्भेदबाधक- (३) अद्वितीयं प्रत्यगभिन्नं ब्रह्म वेदान्तेतरप्रमाणागम्यमिति स्वप्रकाशत्वेन नित्यापरोक्षमिति चार्थः श्रद्धत्स्व सोम्य (छा. ६.१२.२) आचार्यवान् पुरुषो वेद (छा. ६.१४.२) इति गुरुवेदान्तवाक्यश्रद्धामात्रसमधिगम्यत्वबोधकवचनैर्गम्यत इत्यपूर्वता तृतीयं लिङ्गम् ।
Manana is [sustained inquiry into the oneness of jīva and Brahman through reasoning establishing their unity and refuting their difference]. (3) That the non-dual Brahman, non-different from the inner Self, cannot be known by any means of knowledge other than Vedānta, yet is ever immediately evident by virtue of being self-luminous—this meaning is known through statements revealing that It is comprehended solely through faith in the words of the Guru and Vedānta, such as 'Have faith, O gentle one' (Chā. 6.12.2) and 'A man with a teacher knows' (Chā. 6.14.2); hence apūrvatā (unprecedentedness/novelty) is the third indicator.
(४) तस्य तावदेव चिरं यावन्न विमोक्ष्ये अथ सम्पत्स्ये (छा. ६.१४.२) इत्यनेन कार्यकरणसङ्घाताद्व्यावृत्तो ब्रह्मवित् ब्रह्मैव भवतीत्यद्वैतब्रह्मभावापत्तिरूपफलं प्रतिपाद्यत इति फलं चतुर्थं लिङ्गम् ।
(4) By this statement, 'For him there is delay only as long as he is not liberated [from the body], then he shall merge' (Chā. 6.14.2), the fruit consisting in the attainment of the state of non-dual Brahman is propounded—namely, that the knower of Brahman, detached from the aggregate of the physical body and sense-organs, becomes Brahman Itself; therefore, phala (the fruit) is the fourth indicator.
(५) तदैक्षत बहु स्यां प्रजायेय तत्तेजोऽसृजत (छा. ६.२.३) इत्यादिसृष्टिवाक्यैर्भेदनिन्दापूर्वकमभेदः स्तूयत इत्यर्थवादोऽपि पञ्चमं लिङ्गम् ।
(5) Non-difference is eulogised while censuring difference through creation passages such as 'That willed: May I become many, may I multiply; It created fire' (Chā. 6.2.3); therefore, arthavāda (eulogy) is the fifth indicator.
(६) प्रतिपादयिषितस्याद्वैतस्यानुकूलदृष्टान्तप्रदर्शनमुपपत्तिः ।
(6) Upapatti (logical intelligibility) is the demonstration of supporting analogies for the non-duality intended to be expounded.
यथा सोम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृण्मयं विज्ञातं स्याद्वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्येव सत्यम् (छा. ६.१.४) यथा सोम्यैकेन लोहमणिना ॥ (छा. ६.१.५) यथा सोम्यैकेन नखनिकृन्तनेन (छा. ६.१.६) एवमेव खलु सोम्यान्नेन शुङ्गेनापो मूलमन्विच्छाद्भिः सोम्य शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलमन्विच्छ तेजसा सोम्य शुङ्गेन सन्मूलमन्विच्छ सन्मूलाः सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सदायतनाः सत्प्रतिष्ठाः (छा. ६.८.४) इत्यादिवचनैः कारणसद्रूपव्यतिरेकेण कार्यं नास्त्येव, मायामात्रमिदं दृश्यमिति मृल्लोहादिदृष्टान्तमुखेन जगत्सर्वं प्रत्यक्चेतनं ब्रह्मैवेत्युपपत्तिरुच्यत इत्युपपत्तिरपि षष्ठं लिङ्गम् ।
Through statements such as 'Just as, O gentle one, by a single lump of clay all that is made of clay is known—the modification being only a name arising from speech, clay alone is real' (Chā. 6.1.4), 'Just as by a single piece of gold...' (Chā. 6.1.5), 'Just as by a single nail-cutter...' (Chā. 6.1.6), and 'In this very way, O gentle one, through food as the sprout seek water as the root; through water as the sprout seek fire as the root; through fire as the sprout seek Existence as the root. All these creatures, O gentle one, have Existence as their root, Existence as their abode, and Existence as their resting place' (Chā. 6.8.4), the logical rationale is stated that the effect has no existence apart from the causal nature of Existence, that this perceived universe is mere māyā, and that by means of analogies like clay and gold, the entire universe is Brahman alone, the inner Consciousness; therefore, upapatti is the sixth indicator.
एवं उपक्रमोपसंहारादिषड्विधलिङ्गैर्वेदान्तवाक्यानामद्वैते प्रत्यगात्मनि तात्पर्यनिर्णयानुकूलचेतोवृत्तिः श्रवणम् ।
Thus, śravaṇa is the mental modification conducive to determining the purport of the Vedānta statements in the non-dual inner Self by means of the sixfold indicators beginning with upakrama and upasaṃhāra.
एवमेव सर्वेषामपि वेदान्तानामद्वैते तात्पर्यावधारणं बोध्यम् ।
In this very manner, the ascertainment of the purport of all Vedānta texts in non-duality is to be understood.
उपक्रमः = प्रकरणारम्भः, उपसंहारः = प्रकरणसमाप्तिः ।1,2
Upakrama = the beginning of a section; upasaṃhāra = the conclusion of a section.
टिप्पणी
1.
ऐक्यसाधकयुक्तयः- (१) अनुमानप्रमाणं - यत् सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपं न ततो ब्रह्मणो भिद्यते; यत् सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपं न भवति तत् ब्रह्मणो भिद्यते ।
Reasonings establishing identity: (1) Inference (anumāna)—Whatever is of the nature of Existence-Consciousness-Bliss is not different from Brahman; whatever is not of the nature of Existence-Consciousness-Bliss is different from Brahman.
यथेश्वरः सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपत्वादेव ब्रह्मणो न भिद्यते, व्यावहारिको घटादिस्त्वनृतजडदुःखात्मकत्वेन सच्चिदानन्दरूपत्वाभावाद्ब्रह्मणो भिद्यते ।
Just as Īśvara, precisely by virtue of being of the nature of Existence-Consciousness-Bliss, is not different from Brahman, whereas empirical objects like a pot, being of the nature of falsehood, inertness, and suffering, and lacking the nature of Existence-Consciousness-Bliss, differ from Brahman.
एवं जीवोऽपि ब्रह्मैव, सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपत्वात् ईश्वरवत् इत्यनुमानम् ।
In this way, the jīva also is Brahman alone, because of being of the nature of Existence-Consciousness-Bliss, just like Īśvara—this is the inference.
(२) उपमानप्रमाणं - यथा घटाकाशमठाकाशयोर्घटमठरूपोपाधी विना न स्वतो भेदोऽस्ति, तथा अन्तःकरण(बुद्धि) मायारूपोपाधी अन्तरा जीवब्रह्मणोरपि भेदो नैव सिद्ध्यति ।
(2) Comparison (upamāna)—Just as there is no intrinsic difference between pot-space and room-space apart from the limiting adjuncts of pot and room, similarly, apart from the limiting adjuncts of the internal organ (intellect) and māyā, no difference whatsoever is established between jīva and Brahman.
(३) अर्थापत्तिप्रमाणं - नेह नानास्ति किञ्चन (बृ. ४.४.१९, क. २.१.११) ; न तु ततो द्वितीयमस्ति (बृ. ४.३.२३) अतोऽन्यदार्तम् (बृ. ३.७.२३) इत्यादिश्रुत्युक्तभेदनिन्दान्यथानुपपत्त्या वस्तुतोऽभेदासिद्धौ श्रुतिवैयर्थ्यप्रसङ्गादवश्यमैक्यमभ्युपेयम् ।
(3) Presumption (arthāpatti)—Because of the inexplicability otherwise of the censure of difference found in scriptural texts like 'There is no diversity whatsoever here' (Bṛ. 4.4.19, Ka. 2.1.11), 'There is no second entity apart from That' (Bṛ. 4.3.23), and 'Everything other than This is perishable' (Bṛ. 3.7.23), and because otherwise the scripture would be rendered futile if non-difference were not real, identity must necessarily be accepted.
यथा देवदत्तशरीरगतपीनत्वबुद्ध्या भोजनाभावबुद्धिर्बाध्यते, एवं भेदधीरपि नेह नानास्ति (बृ. ४.४.१९, क. २.१.११) नेति नेति (बृ. २-३-६) इत्यादिश्रुतिभिर्बाध्यत एव ।
Just as the idea that Devadatta does not eat is sublated by the cognition of the stoutness of his body, similarly the cognition of difference is certainly sublated by scriptural statements like 'There is no manifold here' (Bṛ. 4.4.19, Ka. 2.1.11) and 'Not this, not this' (Bṛ. 2.3.6).
इदं च युक्तित्रयमभेदसाधकम् ।
And this triad of arguments establishes non-difference.
2.
भेदबाधकयुक्तयः- (१) अनुमानप्रमाणं - प्रत्यक्परचितोर्भेदो मिथ्या, उपाध्यधीनत्वात्, घटा-॥ युक्तिभिः सदाऽद्वितीयब्रह्मात्मैक्यानुसन्धानम् ।
Arguments refuting difference: (1) Inference—The difference between the inner Consciousness and the Supreme Consciousness is illusory, because it is dependent upon limiting adjuncts, like [the space enclosed in] a pot... By such reasonings, one constantly contemplates the oneness of the Self and the non-dual Brahman.
26 · निदिध्यासनलक्षणं
भेदप्रत्यय(अनात्मप्रत्यय)अनन्तरितब्रह्माकारप्रत्ययप्रवाह एव निदिध्यासनं उच्यते ।
The continuous stream of mental modifications shaped like Brahman, uninterrupted by cognitions of difference (i.e. thoughts of the not-Self), is alone called nididhyāsana.
निदिध्यासनपरिपाकावस्थैव समाधिरिति, निदिध्यासनेऽन्तर्भावान्न समाधिः पृथक्साधनत्वेन गण्यते ।
Because samādhi is simply the fully matured state of nididhyāsana, samādhi is not enumerated as a separate means, owing to its inclusion within nididhyāsana.
27 · श्रवणादिप्रयोजननिरूपणं
श्रवणादीनि यद्यपि न साक्षाज्ज्ञानसाधनानि, अप्रमाणत्वात्; तथापि तानि ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धकीभूतबुद्धिदोषासम्भावनाविपरीतभावनादीन् नाशयन्ति ।
Although hearing (*śravaṇa*) and the others are not direct means of knowledge, since they are not independent instruments of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*), nevertheless they destroy the defects of intellect that obstruct knowledge, namely *asambhāvanā* (doubt regarding the validity of the teaching) and *viparītabhāvanā* (contrary conception).
असम्भावना = संशयः ।
*Asambhāvanā* means doubt.
विपरीतभावना = विपर्ययः ।
*Viparītabhāvanā* means error (misapprehension).
काशमठाकाशयोः भेदवत् ।
Just like the difference between pot-space and monastery-space [which is purely conditioned].
यन्नैवं तन्नैवं (यदौपाधिकं न भवति तन्मिथ्या न भवति), यथा व्यावहारिकघटपटादिभेदः औपाधिकस्वाभावादेव सत्यः (न मिथ्या) तद्वत् ।
Whatever is not like this is not like that (that which is not conditioned is not illusory), just as the empirical difference between pot, cloth, etc., being unconditioned, is empirically real (not illusory) in that way.
अत एव यत्र यत्रोपाधिनिबन्धनो भेदस्तत्र तत्र मिथ्यैव सः ।
Therefore, wherever difference is caused by an *upādhi*, in all such cases it is purely illusory.
(२) उपमानप्रमाणं - यथा बिम्बप्रतिबिम्बयोर्भेदो मिथ्या तथा जीवब्रह्मणोरपि ।
(2) The proof from analogy (*upamāna*): Just as the difference between the original object and its reflection is illusory, so too is the difference between the *jīva* and Brahman.
(३) अर्थापत्तिप्रमाणं - महावाक्यैरुपनिषत्सु जीवब्रह्मणोरभेद एव निश्चितः ।
(3) The proof from postulation (*arthāpatti*): In the Upaniṣads, non-difference between the *jīva* and Brahman is definitively established by the *mahāvākyas*.
यदि प्रतीयमानोऽपि भेदो वस्तुतो न मिथ्या स्यात्तर्हि महावाक्यैरभेदो न प्रतिपाद्येत, प्रतिपाद्यते तु ।
If the difference, though perceived, were not in reality illusory, then non-difference would not be taught by the *mahāvākyas*; but it is indeed taught.
तस्मादर्थापत्तिप्रमाणादपि जीवब्रह्मणोर्भेदो मिथ्यैव ।
Therefore, from the proof of postulation (*arthāpatti*) as well, the difference between the *jīva* and Brahman is purely illusory.
(४) अनुपलब्धिप्रमाणं - जाग्रतस्वप्नयोरुपाधेः सत्त्वाज्जीवब्रह्मणोर्भेदः प्रतीयते ।
(4) The proof from non-cognition (*anupalabdhi*): In the waking and dream states, difference between the *jīva* and Brahman is perceived because the *upādhi* is present.
सुषुप्तौ तदभावाद्भेदो नैवोपलभ्यत इत्यतो जीवब्रह्मणोर्भेदः परमार्थतो नैवेति निश्चीयते ।
In deep sleep (*suṣupti*), because that *upādhi* is absent, difference is not perceived at all; hence it is ascertained that ultimately there is no difference whatsoever between the *jīva* and Brahman.
इत्यनुपलब्धिप्रमाणम् ।
Such is the proof from non-cognition (*anupalabdhi*).
एवं एता भेदखण्डनयुक्तयः ।1,2,3,4
Thus, these are the logical arguments refuting difference.
टिप्पणी
1.
अयमेव भेदः साक्षात्कारनिदिध्यासनयोः - स्वयमेव नम्रीभूतवृक्षशाखावद्विनैव स्वप्रयत्नं अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति वेदान्तजन्या अनात्माकारवृत्तिरूपान्तरायरहिता ब्रह्माकारवृत्तिः साक्षात्कार उच्यते ।
This very distinction exists between direct realization (*sākṣātkāra*) and meditation (*nididhyāsana*): Like a tree branch that bends down spontaneously on its own, when the thought-modification of the form of Brahman generated by Vedānta arising without any personal effort—free from the obstacle of thought-modifications of the form of non-Self—arises as I am Brahman, that is called *sākṣātkāra*.
निदिध्यासनं तु स्वप्रयत्नादानमितवृक्षशाखावत्स्वप्रयत्नमात्रसाध्या ब्रह्माकारवृत्तिः ।
*Nididhyāsana*, however, is the mental mode taking the form of Brahman produced strictly by one's own conscious effort, like a tree branch bent down forcefully by effort.
प्रयत्नोपरमे तु शाखाया उन्नमनवत्, निदिध्यासननिवृत्तौ निवर्तेतैव ब्रह्माकारवृत्तिरपि इति ।
Just as a branch springs back up once the effort ceases, so too, upon the cessation of meditation (*nididhyāsana*), the mental mode taking the form of Brahman ceases as well.
2.
अत्र समाधिशब्देन त्रिपुटीभानरहितनिर्विकल्पकसमाधिरभिधीयते ।
Here, by the word *samādhi*, *nirvikalpa-samādhi* (unconditioned absorption) free from the cognition of the triad (*tripuṭī* of meditator, meditation, and object of meditation) is expressed.
निदिध्यासनशब्देन ध्यातृध्यानध्येयात्मकत्रिपुटीयुक्तसविकल्पसमाधिरुच्यते ।
By the word *nididhyāsana*, *savikalpa-samādhi* endowed with the triad of meditator, meditation, and object of meditation is meant.
तथा चोक्तं पञ्चदश्याम् ।
And so it is said in the *Pañcadaśī*:
ताभ्यां निर्विचिकित्सेऽर्थे चेतसः स्थापितस्य यत् । एकतानत्वमेतद्धि निदिध्यासनमुच्यते ॥ ध्यातृध्याने परित्यज्य क्रमात् ध्येयैकगोचरम् । निवातदीपवच्चित्तं समाधिरभिधीयते ॥ (पञ्चदशी तत्त्व. ५४-५५) इति ।
When the mind, established in the object free from doubt by hearing and reflection, attains uninterrupted continuity, this indeed is called *nididhyāsana*. Gradually letting go of the meditator and the act of meditation, when the mind has only the object of meditation (*dhyeya*) as its realm, steady like a lamp in a windless place, it is termed *samādhi*. (Pañcadaśī, Tattvaviveka 54–55)
3.
इयं रज्जुर्वा सर्पो वेति कोटिद्वयविषयकं ज्ञानं संशयः ।
Cognition having two alternative possibilities, such as 'Is this a rope or a snake?', is doubt (*saṁśaya*).
4.
रज्जौ अयं सर्पः इत्यविद्यावृत्तिर्विपर्ययः ।
The *avidyā-vṛtti* taking the form This is a snake with respect to a rope is error (*viparyaya*).
अयमेव भ्रान्तिज्ञानम्, विपरीतभावना, विपरीतज्ञानम्, ज्ञानाध्यास इति चोच्यते ।
This alone is also called *bhrānti-jñāna*, *viparīta-bhāvanā*, *viparīta-jñāna*, and *jñānādhyāsa*.
प्रकृते मिथ्याभूतेषु देहादिष्वनात्मसु सत्यत्वबुद्धिः आत्मत्वबुद्धिश्च विपर्ययः ।
In the present context, the notion of reality (*satyatva-buddhi*) and the notion of Selfhood (*ātmatva-buddhi*) regarding non-Self objects such as the physical body, which are illusory, constitutes error (*viparyaya*).
श्रवणस्योपयोगः - वेदान्तवाक्यं किमद्वितीयं ब्रह्म बोधयति, उत यत्किञ्चिदर्थान्तरमिति प्रमाणगतसन्देहः श्रवणेन निवर्त्यते ।
The utility of *śravaṇa*: The doubt regarding the means of knowledge (*pramāṇa-gata-saṁśaya*), namely 'Do the Vedāntic statements teach non-dual Brahman, or something else?', is dispelled by *śravaṇa*.
मननस्योपयोगः - जीवब्रह्मणोरभेदः सत्य उत भेद इति प्रमेयगतसन्देहः ।
The utility of *manana*: The doubt regarding the knowable object (*prameya-gata-saṁśaya*), namely 'Is the non-difference between the *jīva* and Brahman real, or is difference real?' [is the object of reflection].
स चानेकप्रकारोऽपि मननेन निवार्यते ।
And that doubt, though of manifold varieties, is eliminated by reflection (*manana*).
निदिध्यासनस्योपयोगः - देहादिदृश्यप्रपञ्चः सर्वोऽपि सत्यः, जीवब्रह्मणोर्भेदश्च सत्यः इति धीरविपरीतभावना ।
The utility of *nididhyāsana*: The persistent notion The entire perceptible world beginning with the body is real, and the difference between the *jīva* and Brahman is real is contrary conception (*viparītabhāvanā*).
सा च निदिध्यासनेन निवार्यते ।
And that [contrary conception] is removed by meditation (*nididhyāsana*).
एवं श्रवणादित्रयं ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धकीभूतासम्भावनाविपरीतभावनानिवृत्तिद्वारा परम्परया अपरोक्षज्ञानसाधनं भवति ।
Thus, the triad of hearing and the others serves indirectly as a means to direct knowledge (*aparokṣa-jñāna*) through the elimination of doubt (*asambhāvanā*) and contrary conception (*viparītabhāvanā*) which obstruct knowledge.
न तु साक्षात् ।
And not directly.
28 · अपरोक्षज्ञानसाक्षात्साधनं
ज्ञानस्य साक्षात्साधनं तु श्रोत्रेन्द्रियसम्बद्धवेदान्तवाक्यमेव ।
The direct means of knowledge, however, is indeed the Vedānta sentence connected with the organ of hearing.
तच्च द्विप्रकारम् ।
And that is of two kinds.
अवान्तरवाक्यं महावाक्यं चेति ।
Namely, the intermediate sentence (avāntara-vākya) and the great sentence (mahāvākya).
जीवात्मपरमात्मस्वरूपप्रतिपादकवाक्यमवान्तरवाक्यम् ।
The sentence expounding the nature of the *jīvātman* and the *paramātman* (individually) is the intermediate sentence.
तदैक्यप्रतिपादकवाक्यं महावाक्यमिति चोच्यते ।
And the sentence expounding their identity is called the *mahāvākya*.
अवान्तरवाक्येन परोक्षमेव ज्ञानं जायते ।
Through an intermediate sentence, only mediate (indirect) knowledge arises.
महावाक्येन त्वपरोक्षमेव ।
Whereas through a *mahāvākya*, only direct (immediate) knowledge arises.
अस्ति ब्रह्म इति ज्ञानं परोक्षम् ।
The cognition 'Brahman exists' is indirect knowledge.
अहमेव ब्रह्म इति ज्ञानमपरोक्षम् ।
The cognition 'I myself am Brahman' is direct knowledge.
त्वमेव ब्रह्मासि इति गुरूपदिष्टमहावाक्यश्रवणानन्तरं श्रोतुः शिष्यस्य पुष्कलसाधनसम्पन्नस्य अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इत्यपरोक्षमेव ज्ञानं जायते ।
Immediately upon hearing the *mahāvākya* taught by the *guru*—'You yourself are Brahman'—there arises only direct knowledge 'I am Brahman' for the listening disciple who is endowed with full spiritual qualifications.
श्रोत्रेणासम्बद्धं वाक्यं नैव ज्ञानं जनयेत् ।
A sentence not connected with the ear cannot produce knowledge at all.
अतः श्रोत्रेन्द्रियसम्बद्धमहावाक्यमेवापरोक्षज्ञानहेतुः ।
Therefore, only the *mahāvākya* connected with the sense of hearing is the cause of direct knowledge.
महावाक्येन सर्वेषां ज्ञानमपरोक्षमेव जायते, न तु परोक्षमिति नियमः ।
The invariable rule is that through the *mahāvākya*, knowledge arises as direct alone for everyone, never as indirect.
(A. 29-31) महावाक्यमपरोक्षज्ञानहेतुरित्यत्राक्षेपसमाधानानि
(Avartas 29–31) Objections and resolutions on the point that the *mahāvākya* is the cause of direct knowledge.
टिप्पणी
1.
प्रमाणं = उपनिषद्वाक्यानि, शब्दप्रमाणम् ।
Pramāṇa = the Upaniṣadic statements, verbal testimony.
2.
प्रमेयः = मोक्षादिज्ञेयविषयः ।
Prameya = the knowable subject matter such as liberation.
3.
एवं संशयद्वये निवृत्तेऽपि साक्षात्कारात्पूर्वमविद्यायाः सत्त्वात् अहं ब्रह्म न भवामि, जीव एवाहं; मत्तो भिन्नमेव ब्रह्म; देहादिजगत् सत्यम्; इत्येवंविधानेकसंशयाः [विपर्ययाः] पुनः पुनर्जायेरन् ।
Even when both kinds of doubt have been dispelled, because of the existence of *avidyā* prior to direct realization, many such doubts [and misconceptions] may arise again and again, such as: 'I am not Brahman, I am merely a *jīva*; Brahman is completely distinct from me; the world starting with the body is real.'
तन्निवृत्तये सदा निदिध्यासितव्यमेव ।
For their removal, one must constantly practise *nididhyāsana*.
4.
नेत्राञ्जनं नेत्ररोगनिवृत्तिद्वारा सूर्यावलोकने उपकरोति नेत्रस्य ।
Eye-salve assists the eye in seeing the sun by way of removing eye disease.
नेत्रमेव तु सूर्यं साक्षाद्यथा पश्यति, तथा श्रवणादीन्यपि ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धकीभूतसंशयविपर्ययरूप(दोष)रोगनिवृत्तिद्वारा ब्रह्मज्ञानसाधनानि भवन्ति ।
Just as the eye alone directly sees the sun (while the collyrium merely removes impediments), likewise *śravaṇa* and the rest serve as aids to the knowledge of Brahman through the removal of the defect (disease) in the form of doubt and error that obstructs knowledge.
साक्षाज्ज्ञानसाधनं तु श्रोत्रसम्बद्धमहावाक्यमेव ।
The direct means of knowledge, however, is solely the *mahāvākya* connected with the ear.
समाधानम्महावाक्यमपरोक्षज्ञानहेतुरित्यत्राक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ २९–३१ ॥
29 · अत्र केचिदाक्षिपन्ति
(१) श्रवणादीनि महावाक्यानि च समुच्चित्यैवापरोक्षज्ञानं जनयन्ति ।
(1) Only by combining *śravaṇa* and the rest along with the *mahāvākya*s do they generate direct knowledge.
केवलानि तु वाक्यानि परोक्षमेव ज्ञानं जनयेयुः, नापरोक्षम् ।
The sentences on their own, however, can produce only mediate knowledge, not immediate knowledge.
(२) केवलवाक्यान्येव यद्यपरोक्षज्ञानं जनयेयुस्तर्हि व्यर्थानि स्युः श्रवणमनननिदिध्यासनानीति ।
(2) If mere sentences alone were to produce direct knowledge, then hearing (*śravaṇa*), reflection (*manana*), and contemplation (*nididhyāsana*) would become utterly futile.
न च केवलमहावाक्यादपरोक्षमेव ज्ञानं जायते, श्रवणादीनां त्वसम्भावनाविपरीतभावनानिवृत्तावुपयुक्तत्वान्न व्यर्थतेति वाच्यम् ।
Nor can it be argued: 'Direct knowledge arises from the *mahāvākya* alone, and *śravaṇa* etc. are not futile because they are useful in removing the sense of impossibility (*asambhāvanā*) and contrary conviction (*viparītabhāvanā*).'
अपरोक्षज्ञानविषये वस्तुनि कस्याप्यसम्भावनाविपरीतभावनानुदयात्, केवलादपि महावाक्यादपरोक्षमेव ज्ञानं जायत इति वदतां मते, तत्त्वमस्यादिमहावाक्यैर्ब्रह्मापरोक्षज्ञानोत्पत्त्यनन्तरमसम्भावनाविपरीतभावनानुत्पत्तेः श्रवणादिसाधनानां व्यर्थतैव स्यात् ।
Because in an object of direct cognition neither impossibility nor contrary belief can arise for anyone, in the view of those who hold that direct knowledge arises from the solitary *mahāvākya* alone, after direct knowledge of Brahman is generated through *mahāvākya*s like 'Tat Tvam Asi', impossibility and contrary conviction could never arise, and therefore the disciplines such as *śravaṇa* would indeed be entirely useless.
अस्मन्मते तु (पूर्वपक्षिमते) केवलवाक्येन परोक्षमेव ज्ञानं प्रथमं जायते ।
In our view, however (the pūrvapakṣin's position), by the sentence alone only indirect knowledge arises initially.
श्रवणादिसहकृतेन वाक्येन तु पश्चादपरोक्षमित्यङ्गीकारान्न श्रवणादिवैयर्थ्यम् ।
And because we accept that direct knowledge arises subsequently through the sentence aided by *śravaṇa* and the rest, there is no futility of *śravaṇa* etc.
इत्यनेकग्रन्थकृत्तात्पर्यमिति ।
Such is the purport of several commentators.
30 · प्रथमाक्षेपस्य समाधानं
यदुक्तं शब्दसामान्यं परोक्षमेव ज्ञानं जनयेदिति, नैतत्साधु ।
As to what was stated—that verbal testimony in general can produce only mediate knowledge—this is not correct.
यतोऽयमेव स्वभावः शब्दस्य यत् परोक्षापरोक्षरूपद्विविधज्ञानजनकत्वमिति ।
Because this alone is the nature of verbal testimony: namely, the capacity to generate two kinds of knowledge, mediate and immediate.
देशकालपरिच्छिन्नं (आवृतम्) वस्तु व्यवहितमित्युच्यते ।
An entity delimited by space and time (i.e. veiled/separated) is called 'remote' (*vyavahita*).
तदनवच्छिन्नं (तदनावृतम्) अव्यवहितमिति च ।
And that which is not delimited by those (i.e. not veiled) is called 'immediate' (*avyavahita*).
व्यवहितविषयकं शाब्दं ज्ञानं परोक्षमेव, न कदाचित् कथञ्चिदप्यपरोक्षं भवति; स्वर्गेन्द्रदेवतादीनां व्यवहितानां ज्ञानस्य शास्त्ररूपशब्दप्रमाणेन जायमानस्य नित्यं परोक्षत्वात् ।
Verbal cognition regarding a remote object is always mediate only; it never in any way becomes immediate; because the knowledge of remote entities such as heaven, Indra, and the gods, generated through the verbal means of knowledge in the form of scripture, is invariably mediate.
अव्यवहितवस्तुविषयकं शाब्दं ज्ञानं परोक्षमपरोक्षं च भवति ।
Verbal cognition regarding an immediate object can be both mediate and immediate.
यदा अव्यवहितवस्तुविषयकं ज्ञानं अस्ति इति शब्देन जायते तदा अव्यवहितस्यापि वस्तुनो ज्ञानं परोक्षमेव भवति ।
When knowledge regarding an immediate object is produced by the word 'exists' (*asti*), then the knowledge of even an immediate object is mediate only.
यथा दशमोऽस्ति इत्यत्र अस्ति शब्देन जायमानमव्यवहितस्यापि दशमपुरुषस्य ज्ञानं परोक्षमेव भवति ।
Just as in 'The tenth person exists', the knowledge of the tenth person produced by the word 'exists' is mediate only, even though he is immediate.
यदा अव्यवहितवस्तुविषयकं ज्ञानं इदमस्ति इत्यादि शब्दप्रमाणेन जायते तदा तज्ज्ञानमपरोक्षमेव भवति, न परोक्षम् ।
When knowledge regarding an immediate object arises by means of words such as 'This exists', then that knowledge is direct (immediate) only, not mediate.
यथा ।1,2,3
For example:
टिप्पणी
1.
पञ्चदशप्रकरणादिकृद्विद्यारण्यप्रभृतयः ।
[This is maintained by] Vidyāraṇya, the author of the fifteen treatises (Pañcadaśī) and other texts, and others.
2.
इदं शारीरकमीमांसायास्तात्पर्यम् ।
This is the purport of the Śārīraka-Mīmāṁsā.
3.
दूरदेशे स्थितं वस्तु देशतो व्यवहितम् ।
An object situated in a distant place is spatially remote (*deśataḥ vyavahitam*).
भूतभविष्यद्वस्तु कालतो व्यवहितमित्युच्यते ।
An object belonging to the past or future is called temporally remote (*kālataḥ vyavahitam*).
दशमस्त्वमसि इत्यत्र त्वमसि शब्देन जायमानं दशमपुरुषज्ञानमपरोक्षमेव भवति ।
In the statement 'You are the tenth', the knowledge of the tenth person generated by the words 'you are' (*tvam asi*) is direct (immediate) only.
एवमेव प्रकृतस्य ब्रह्मणः सर्वप्राणिप्रत्यगात्मभूतत्वादत्यन्ताव्यवहितस्य नित्यापरोक्षरूपस्यापि ज्ञानम्, तदस्ति इत्यवान्तरवाक्येन परोक्षमेव जायते ।
In the very same way, although Brahman under consideration is absolutely immediate and eternally direct because of being the inner Self of all living beings, its knowledge generated by the intermediate sentence 'That exists' (*tat asti*) is mediate only.
महावाक्यं तु दशमस्त्वमसि इतिवत् श्रोतुरात्मत्वेनापरोक्षतया ब्रह्म बोधयति ।
The Mahāvākya, however, reveals Brahman directly as the hearer's own Self, just like 'You are the tenth'.
अत एव महावाक्येनाव्यवहितप्रत्यग्ब्रह्मापरोक्षज्ञानमेव जायते, न तु परोक्षमिति ।
Therefore, by the Mahāvākya, only the immediate knowledge of the unseparated inner Brahman is generated, not mediate knowledge.
31 · द्वितियाक्षेपस्य समाधानं
यत्तूक्तं महावाक्येनापरोक्षज्ञानोत्पत्यङ्गीकारेऽपरोक्षज्ञानोत्पत्यधिकरणेऽसम्भावनाद्यनुत्पत्तेः श्रवणादीनां वैयर्थ्यं स्यादिति, तदसत् ।
As for what was argued — that if the rise of direct knowledge from the *mahāvākya* is accepted, then because doubts such as impossibility cannot arise in the locus where direct knowledge has arisen, *śravaṇa* and the rest would become futile — that is invalid.
कश्चन राजा स्वामात्यं भर्च्छुनामकं चक्षुषा पश्यन्नपि विपरीतभावनया यथा न विवेद तम्, तथा महावाक्येन ब्रह्मापरोक्षज्ञानोत्पत्तावपि यस्यान्तःकरणे असम्भावनादिदोषाः प्रतिबन्धकाः वर्तन्ते तस्य सकलङ्कं ज्ञानं नैव फलाय कल्पते ।
Just as a certain king, even while seeing his own minister named Bharchu with his eyes, did not recognise him because of a contrary conviction (*viparīta-bhāvanā*), even so, upon the arising of direct knowledge of Brahman through the *mahāvākya*, for one in whose mind defects such as *asambhāvanā* persist as obstacles, his tainted knowledge does not yield its fruit (*mokṣa*).
अतः प्रतिबन्धकीभूतदोषनिवृत्त्यर्थं तेन श्रवणादिकमवश्यमावर्तनीयम् ।
Therefore, in order to remove the defects that act as obstacles, *śravaṇa* and the rest must necessarily be practiced repeatedly by him.
यस्य तु पुनर्बुद्धौ महाभाग्यवशात् रागद्वेषादिकारणीभूतासम्भावनादिदोषा नैव विद्यन्ते तस्य श्रवणादिवैयर्थ्यमिष्टमेव ।
On the other hand, for one in whose intellect defects such as *asambhāvanā* (which are caused by attachment and aversion) do not exist at all due to great merit, the futility of *śravaṇa* etc. is entirely acceptable (*iṣṭa*).
एवञ्च ज्ञानस्य साक्षात्कारणं महावाक्यमेव, न श्रवणादि ।
And thus, the direct instrument of knowledge is the *mahāvākya* alone, not *śravaṇa* etc.
श्रवणादि तु ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धकीभूतासम्भावनादिदोषापनयनमात्रं कुर्यात् ।
*Śravaṇa* and the rest merely effect the removal of the defects such as *asambhāvanā* that obstruct knowledge.
तावन्मात्रेण श्रवणाद्यपि ज्ञानसाधनमिति गौण्या वृत्त्योच्यते ।
Merely to that extent is *śravaṇa* etc. also spoken of as a 'means of knowledge' in a secondary, figurative sense (*gauṇī vṛtti*).
तथा च विवेकादिचतुष्टयमपि श्रवणाद्युपकारकतया ज्ञानसाधनमित्येवोच्यते ।
And likewise, the fourfold discipline beginning with discrimination (*viveka*) is also spoken of as a means of knowledge only in the sense of being an aid to *śravaṇa* etc.
तथा च विवेकादिसाधनचतुष्टयसम्पन्न एवाधिकारीति सिद्धम् ।1,2,3
And so it is established that only one endowed with the fourfold means beginning with discrimination is the qualified aspirant (*adhikārin*).
टिप्पणी
1.
दशमपुरुषकथा - दश पथिका देशान्तरगमनसमये मध्ये मार्गे काञ्चिन्नदीं गभीरां प्राप्य एकैकशस्तीर्त्वा परं पारमासाद्य सर्वे वयमुत्तीर्णा न वेति सन्दिहानास्तत्प्रत्ययार्थं प्रत्येकं स्वात्मानं विहाय गणयन्तः नवैव वयं स्मः एको नद्यां ममार इति रुरुदुः ।
The Story of the Tenth Man — Ten travellers, while traveling to another country, came across a deep river on their way, swam across one by one, and upon reaching the opposite bank, doubted whether they had all crossed or not. To verify this, each one counted leaving out himself, and thinking 'We are only nine; one has drowned in the river', they began to weep.
तदा कश्चन पान्थः तेषां परिदेवनं श्रुत्वा, बुद्ध्वा च दुःखनिदानं, कृपया प्रथमतः दशमोऽस्ति इत्यवोचत् ।
Then a certain passerby, hearing their lamentation and understanding the cause of their grief, out of compassion first said, 'The tenth man exists.'
तदा तेषां परोक्षमेव ज्ञानं दशमविषयमभूत् ।
Then they had only indirect knowledge regarding the tenth person.
तेष्वेकः कुत्रास्ति दशमः इत्यपृच्छत् ।
One among them asked, 'Where is the tenth man?'
सोऽब्रवीत् स दशमः त्वमसि इति ।
He said: 'You are that tenth man.'
तदैव तस्य स्वविषयकदशमत्वज्ञानमपरोक्षमेवाजायत ।
At that very instant, direct (*aparokṣa*) knowledge of being the tenth man arose in him regarding himself.
तथा चापरोक्ष्ये सत्यपि दशमस्य, करणे च चक्षुषि सति, दशमस्त्वमसि इति परोपदेशमन्तरा स्वविषयकं ज्ञानं परोक्षकल्पमेवासीत् ।
And thus, even though the tenth man was directly present and the eye as an instrument was present, without the instruction of another — 'You are the tenth' — the knowledge regarding himself remained as if indirect.
यथैवात्र त्वमेवासि दशमः इत्याप्तोपदिष्टवाक्यमपरोक्षज्ञाने साक्षात्स्वयं करणम्, एवमेव प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मापरोक्षज्ञानेऽपि गुरूपदिष्टमहावाक्यमपि साक्षादेव करणं भवति ।
Just as here the trustworthy statement 'You yourself are the tenth' is itself the direct instrument for immediate knowledge, in the very same way, regarding the direct knowledge of the inner Brahman, the *mahāvākya* taught by the Guru is itself the direct instrument.
तस्य च संशयादिदोषप्रतिबन्धकशून्यशुद्धान्तःकरणं सहकारिसाधनम् ।
And a pure mind, freed from the obstructing defects such as doubt, is its auxiliary cause (*sahakāri-sādhana*).
(चतुर्थस्तरङ्गे अस्य विस्तरः)
(The elaboration of this is in the fourth Wave.)
2.
इयं कथा पञ्चमतरङ्गे विव्रियते ।
This story is explained in detail in the fifth Wave.
3.
अयं पुरुषो वेदान्तग्रन्थे तद्विचारद्वारा आत्मज्ञाने आत्मज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षे च अधिक्रियते ।
This person is entitled to the Vedantic text, through inquiry into it to Self-knowledge, and through Self-knowledge to liberation (*mokṣa*).
32 · विषयनिरूपणं
अयं च ग्रन्थो जीवब्रह्मैक्यं प्रतिपादयति ।
And this treatise expounds the identity of the *jīva* and Brahman.
अतः प्रत्यक्परचितोरैक्यमेवास्य ग्रन्थस्य विषयः ।
Therefore, the identity of the inner Consciousness and the Supreme Consciousness is alone the subject-matter (*viṣaya*) of this treatise.
सर्वे वेदास्तमेवार्थं प्रतिपादयन्ति ।
All the Vedas propound that very same truth.
इतोऽन्यथा द्वैतवादिनो वेदविरुद्धार्थवादित्वाद्वेदबाह्याः शठाः = गूढविप्रियकारिणः = प्रत्यक्षं स्तुतिकर्तारः परोक्षे चातिदूषकाः । (A. 33-38) प्रयोजननिरूपणम्-
Contrary to this, the dualists (*dvaitavādins*), because they preach doctrines opposed to the Vedas, are outside the Vedic fold and are hypocrites (*śaṭhāḥ*) — that is, they work secret harm, praising in front while severely reviling behind the back. (Āvartas 33–38: Determination of the Purpose / *Prayojana*).
प्रयोजननिरूपणम्॥ ३३–३८ ॥
33 · प्रयोजनलक्षणं
सर्वप्रपञ्चकारणीभूताज्ञानं तत्कार्यदृश्यजातं सर्वं द्वैतं च जननमरणप्रबन्धरूपाखिलदुःखनिदानत्वान्महानर्थ इति श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणेतिहासानुभवादिसकलप्रमाणसिद्धम् ।
That avidyā which is the cause of the entire phenomenal world, all its perceived effects, and indeed all duality constitutes a great evil because it is the root cause of all sorrow in the form of the continuous cycle of birth and death — this is established by all valid means of knowledge including Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇa, Itihāsa, and direct experience.
ईदृशानर्थनिवृत्तिः परमानन्दावाप्तिश्च मोक्ष इत्युच्यते ।
The cessation of such calamity and the attainment of supreme bliss is called mokṣa.
अयमेव मोक्षोऽस्य ग्रन्थस्य परमप्रयोजनम् ।
This very mokṣa is the supreme purpose (parama-prayojana) of this treatise.
ज्ञानं त्ववान्तरप्रयोजनम् ।
Knowledge, however, is the intermediate purpose (avāntara-prayojana).
पुरुषस्य यद्विषये उत्कटेच्छा जायते तदेव तस्य परमं प्रयोजनं पुरुषार्थ इति चोच्यते ।
That with respect to which an intense desire arises in a person is alone called his supreme purpose, or the human goal (puruṣārtha).
सकलजनानां च दुःखनिवृत्तौ सुखावाप्तौ चेदृशीच्छा सञ्जायते ।
And such an intense desire arises in all people regarding the cessation of sorrow and the attainment of happiness.
पूर्वोक्तानर्थद्वैताभावोपलक्षितपरमानन्दचिदेव मोक्षस्वरूपम् ।
The essential nature of mokṣa is simply the supreme *ānanda*-consciousness indicated by the absence of the aforementioned calamitous duality.
अत एव मोक्षः परमप्रयोजनं, न ज्ञानम् ।
Therefore, mokṣa is the supreme purpose, not knowledge.
दुःखनिवृत्तावानन्दावाप्तौ च ज्ञानस्य हेतुत्वात्, तस्य दुःखनिवृत्यानन्दरूपत्वाभावाच्च ज्ञानमवान्तरप्रयोजनम् ।
Because knowledge is the means to the cessation of sorrow and the attainment of bliss, and because it is not itself of the nature of the cessation of sorrow or bliss, knowledge is the intermediate purpose.
परमप्रयोजनावाप्तौ यत् द्वारीभवति तदवान्तरप्रयोजनम् ।
Whatever serves as an intermediate means in the attainment of the supreme purpose is the secondary/intermediate purpose.
यथा कदलीफलप्राप्तौ तत्पत्रपुष्पादि ।
Just as in the acquisition of banana fruit, its leaves, flowers, and the like (serve as intermediate fruits/means).
एतादृशवेदान्तग्रन्थजनितज्ञानद्वारा मुक्तिरूपपरमप्रयोजनफलप्राप्तौ ज्ञानमवान्तरप्रयोजनं भवति ।
In the attainment of the ultimate fruit of liberation by means of the knowledge generated by such a Vedānta treatise, knowledge serves as the intermediate purpose.
34 · अत्र प्रथमाक्षेपः
यदुक्तमनर्थनिवृत्तिः परमानन्दावाप्तिश्च ग्रन्थस्य परमप्रयोजनमिति, तन्न सङ्गच्छते ।
That which was stated — namely, that the cessation of calamity and the attainment of supreme bliss is the supreme purpose of this treatise — is not tenable.
यतः सर्वेष्वपि वेदान्तेषु जीवस्य परमानन्दरूपत्वं वर्णितम् ।
For in all the Upaniṣads, the jīva is described as being of the very nature of supreme *ānanda*.
भवद्भिरपि तथैवाङ्गीकृतम् ।
And it has been accepted by you in the very same way.
लोके त्वप्राप्तस्यैव प्राप्तिर्युज्यते ।
In common experience, however, attainment is reasonable only of that which has not already been attained.
न तु सदा प्राप्तस्यैव प्राप्तिः कदाचिदपि सङ्गच्छते ।
The attainment of what is already ever-attained never makes sense at any time.
तस्मात्सदा परमानन्दस्वरूपस्यैव सत आत्मनः पुनः परमानन्दप्राप्तिकथनं सर्वथाप्यसम्भावितमेवेति ।
Therefore, asserting the 'attainment of supreme bliss' for the Ātman, which is itself already ever of the nature of supreme *ānanda*, is completely impossible in every way.'
35 · तत्समाधिः
एतादृशपूर्वपक्ष्याक्षेपश्रवणमात्रेणाद्वैतग्रन्थोक्तप्रयोजनेऽनादरो न कार्यः ।
One should not disregard the purpose stated in the Advaita treatises merely upon hearing such objections of the opponent.
वेदान्तज्ञानोपदेष्टृसद्गुरुकृपालेशपात्रीभूतानामीदृशाशेषसन्देहतूलनिरासस्य दृष्टान्तप्रचण्डवातबलेन सुकरत्वात् ।
Because for those who have become recipients of even a fraction of the grace of a true Guru imparting Vedāntic knowledge, blowing away all such cotton-like doubts is easily accomplished by the power of the fierce gale of illustrations.
तथा हि, कश्चन पुरुषो भ्रान्त्या स्वकरस्थकङ्कणं नष्टं मत्वा अन्वेषमाण इतस्ततो भ्रमन्1,2
To explain: a person, mistakenly thinking that the bracelet on his own wrist is lost, wanders here and there searching for it...
टिप्पणी
1.
जीवशब्देन जीवशब्दलक्ष्यार्थः कूटस्थो बोध्यः ।
By the word jīva, the immutable Consciousness (kūṭastha), which is the implied sense (lakṣyārtha) of the term jīva, is to be understood.
2.
विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्म (बृ. ३.९.२७) इत्याद्यनन्तश्रुतयः ।
There are endless Śruti passages such as 'Brahman is consciousness and bliss' (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.9.27).
अस्यार्थस्तु विज्ञानं जीवचैतन्यम्, आनन्दं ब्रह्मैव न ततोऽतिरिच्यत इति ।
The meaning of this is: 'consciousness' is the consciousness of the jīva, which is itself nothing other than Brahman that is 'bliss'.
अन्येन केनचिदाप्तेन प्रबोधितः सन्, प्राप्तमेव करस्थं कङ्कणमपूर्वतया प्राप्तमिति मन्यमानः मम कङ्कणमिदानीमुपलब्धम् इति यथा वदति; तथैव परमानन्दस्वरूपे स्वात्मनि नित्यापरोक्षतया सदा प्राप्तेऽप्यविद्यावशादप्राप्तत्वभ्रान्त्या नाहं परमानन्दस्वरूपः, किन्तु ब्रह्मैव तथा; ततो विलक्षणस्य मम तदुपासनया तादृशब्रह्मप्राप्तिः सम्पाद्या इति मूढो भ्रान्त्या प्रतिपद्यते ।
Just as a person awakened by a trustworthy friend, thinking that the bracelet already on his wrist has been newly obtained, says 'My bracelet is found now'; similarly, even though one's own Self is ever-attained and eternally immediate as supreme bliss, a deluded person through the misconception of non-attainment due to avidyā thinks: 'I am not of the nature of supreme bliss, but Brahman alone is such; and I, being different from That, must achieve the attainment of such Brahman by meditating on It.'
एवंवित् पण्डितोऽपि मूढतम एव ।
Even a scholar who thinks thus is exceedingly foolish.
अन्योऽसावन्योऽहमस्मीति न स वेद यथा पशुः (बृ. १.४.१०) तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते (के. १.४.८) योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते । किं तेन न कृतं पापं चौरेणात्मापहारिणा इत्यादिश्रुतिस्मृतिशतेभ्यो जीवब्रह्मभेदवादिनां मूर्खत्वाङ्गीकारात् ।
For hundreds of Śruti and Smṛti texts — such as 'He who thinks He is another and I am another knows not; he is like a beast' (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.4.10), 'Know that alone to be Brahman, not this which they worship here' (Kena Upaniṣad 1.4.8), and 'He who conceives the Self, existing in one way, to be otherwise — what sin has not been committed by that thief who robs the Self?' — explicitly accept that those who maintain difference between jīva and Brahman are foolish.
इत्थंभूतानामपि मूर्खाणामनन्तजन्मार्जितपुण्यपुञ्जवशात्संस्कृतचित्तानाम्, प्रशान्तचित्तात् ब्रह्मविद्वरिष्ठात् सद्गुरोर्यदि कदाचिद्वेदान्तश्रवणं लभ्येत, तदा परमानन्दो वेदान्तवाक्यैः सद्गुरुकृपाकटाक्षलेशेन चास्माभिः प्राप्तः इति मतिर्जायेत ।
If such deluded individuals, having their minds purified by the accumulated merit of countless births, should happen to listen to Vedānta from a noble Guru who is serene of mind and the foremost of the knowers of Brahman, then the conviction arises: 'Supreme bliss has been attained by us through the statements of Vedānta and through a fraction of the gracious glance of the noble Guru.'
अयं भावः - आत्मनः परमानन्दस्वरूपत्वेऽपि स्वप्रकाशापरोक्षस्वरूपत्वेऽपि स्वाविद्यावृतत्वादप्राप्तवत्तेषां स्वस्वरूपं पूर्वमभात् ।
The import is this: although the Self is intrinsically supreme bliss, self-luminous, and immediately evident, it previously appeared to them as if unobtained because it was veiled by their own avidyā.
यदा तु श्रीमदाचार्यमुखाद्वेदान्तश्रवणेन स्वस्वरूपभूत एव परमानन्दो बुद्धाववभासते तदैव स अपूर्वतया प्राप्तवद्व्यवह्रियते ।
When, however, through hearing Vedānta from the mouth of the revered Teacher, the supreme bliss that is one's own real nature shines forth in the intellect, then alone it is treated conventionally as if it were attained anew.
एवमेव प्राप्तस्यापि पुनः प्राप्तिकथनमुपपद्यते ।
In this way alone is the description of the 'attainment of the already-attained' logically justified.
तस्मात्परमानन्दप्राप्तिरेवास्य ग्रन्थस्य परमप्रयोजनमिति युक्तमेवोक्तम् ।
Therefore, it is rightly said that the attainment of supreme bliss is indeed the ultimate purpose (parama-prayojana) of this treatise.
36
प्राप्तप्राप्तिरूपप्रयोजनं निरूप्येदानीं नित्यनिवृत्तनिवृत्तिरूपप्रयोजनमपि युक्तमेवोक्तमित्युच्यते ।
Having explained the purpose in the form of attaining what is already attained, it is now stated that the purpose consisting in the cessation of that which is already eternally ceased is also stated quite properly.
रज्जौ सर्पस्य नित्यनिवृत्तस्यापि कदाचिद्भ्रमादवभासे सति, रज्जुरेवेयम् इत्यधिष्ठानसाक्षात्कारमात्रेण स निवर्तते यथा, तथा स्वात्मनि भ्रमात् प्रतीयमानोऽपि संसारः, नित्यनिवृत्त एव स्वस्वरूपारोक्षसाक्षात्कारेण निश्शेषं निवर्तते ।
Just as when the snake, which is eternally non-existent in the rope, appears due to illusion, it ceases merely through the direct perception of the substratum in the form 'this is only a rope', so too *saṃsāra*, though appearing in one's own *ātman* due to delusion, is ever-ceased and ceases completely by the direct realization of one's own essential nature.
तस्मान्1नित्यनिवृत्तस्यापि
Therefore, even of that which is eternally ceased...
टिप्पणी
1.
व्यावहारिकदशायां प्रातिभासिकदशायाञ्चावभासमानस्यापि प्रपञ्चस्य नेति नेति (बृ. २.३.६) अतोऽन्यदार्तम् (बृ. ३.७.२३) न तु तद्द्वितीयमस्ति ततोऽन्यद्विभक्तम् (बृ. ४.३.२३) नेह नानास्ति किञ्चन (बृ. ४.४.१९) इत्यादिश्रुतिभिः युक्तिभिः स्वानुभवैश्च परमार्थतोऽविद्यमानत्वमेव ।
Of the universe which appears in the empirical and illusory states, there is absolute non-existence in ultimate reality, as established by Śruti passages such as 'Not this, not this' (Bṛ. 2.3.6), 'Whatever is other than this is perishable' (Bṛ. 3.7.23), 'There is no second thing distinct and separate from that' (Bṛ. 4.3.23), 'There is no manifold diversity here at all' (Bṛ. 4.4.19), as well as through reasoning and personal experience.
कालत्रयनिषेध एव नित्यनिवृत्तिरित्युच्यते ।
Negation across the three periods of time (past, present, future) alone is called 'eternal cessation' (*nityanivṛtti*).
पूर्वोक्तप्रमाणैः कालत्रयेऽपि प्रपञ्चो नास्त्येवेति प्रपञ्चयाथात्म्यनिश्चय एव नित्यनिवृत्तस्य तस्य निवृत्तिर्ज्ञेया ।
By the aforementioned pramāṇas, the ascertainment of the true nature of the world as 'the world never exists at all in the three periods of time' alone is to be understood as the cessation of that which is already eternally ceased.
निवृत्तिः, नित्यप्राप्तस्यापि प्राप्तिश्च वेदान्तग्रन्थस्य परमप्रयोजनं सुतरामुपपन्नमेव ।
Thus, cessation (of what is already ceased) and the attainment of what is already eternally attained are entirely well-established as the supreme purpose of the Vedānta treatise.
37 · द्वितीयाक्षेपः
ननु सविलासाज्ञाननिवृत्तिः परमानन्दावाप्तिश्च ग्रन्थस्य प्रयोजनमित्युक्तं न सङ्गच्छते ।
[Objection:] Indeed, what was stated—that the purpose of the treatise is the cessation of ignorance along with its effects and the attainment of supreme bliss—does not hold good.
यतो निवृत्तिर्नाम निश्शेषनाश एव; नाशस्तु प्रध्वंसाभाव एव ।
Because cessation is verily complete destruction; and destruction is nothing but posterior non-existence (*pradhvaṃsābhāva*).
अतोऽनर्थनिवृत्तिरूपाभावस्य परमानन्दप्राप्तिरूपभावस्य चैकत्र मुक्तिस्वरूपे सामानाधिकरण्यं न घटेत, भावाभावयोरन्योन्यविरोधात्, विरुद्धधर्मयोरेकत्र युगपत्समावेशायोगाच्च ।
Therefore, co-existence in a single locus—namely, the nature of liberation—cannot occur between the negative entity (the cessation of evil) and the positive entity (the attainment of supreme bliss), because positive and negative entities are mutually contradictory, and two contradictory attributes cannot co-exist simultaneously in one and the same locus.
तस्मादुक्तप्रयोजनं ग्रन्थस्य न सम्भवतीति चेत्-
Therefore, if it be objected that the stated purpose of the treatise is not possible—
38 · तत्समाधिः
नैष दोषः ।
This defect does not arise.
सविलासाविद्यानिवृत्तेरधिष्ठानब्रह्मचैतन्यमात्रत्वान्न ततोऽतिरिच्यते सा ।
Because the cessation of avidyā along with its effects is nothing other than its substratum, the consciousness that is Brahman, it is not distinct from it.
यथा आरोपितसर्पनिवृत्तिरधिष्ठानरज्जुमात्रम्, एवं कल्पितनामरूपात्मकसकलवस्तुनिवृत्तिरपि तदधिष्ठानचिन्मात्रमेव, न ततोऽतिरिक्तेति सिद्धम् ।
Just as the cessation of the superimposed snake is nothing other than the substratum rope, likewise the cessation of all objects possessing imagined names and forms is also nothing other than their substratum, pure consciousness alone, and is not distinct from it — this stands established.
आरोपितप्रतियोगिकप्रध्वंसस्य प्रतियोग्यधिष्ठाने भासमानस्याधिष्ठानमात्रत्वनियमात् ।
This is because of the universal rule that the posterior non-existence (destruction) of an imagined entity appearing upon the substratum of that counterpositive is nothing other than the substratum itself.
तदुक्तं वार्तिके अधिष्ठानावशेषो हि नाशः कल्पितवस्तुनः इति ।
Thus it has been said in the Vārttika: 'The destruction of an imagined entity is indeed its remaining as the substratum alone.'
अयमेव भगवत्पादादीनामाशयः आकरादिषु स्फुटतरः ।
This very intent of Śrī Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda and others is abundantly clear in the foundational texts.
अत एव प्रकृतेऽप्यनर्थनिवृत्तिर्ब्रह्ममात्रमित्युक्तदोषानवकाशः ।
Therefore, in the present context as well, because the cessation of suffering is nothing other than Brahman alone, there is no scope for the aforementioned defect.
सर्वानर्थदृश्यकल्पनाधिष्ठानत्वाद्ब्रह्मणः ।
For Brahman is the substratum for the conceptual superimposition of all evils and visible phenomena.
तच्च ब्रह्म सिद्धवस्तुस्वरूपत्वाद्भावरूपम् ।
And that Brahman, being an already existent reality by nature, is positive in form (not a mere absence).
तस्मादनर्थनिवृत्तेर्भावरूपत्वादेव तस्या अस्मिन् ग्रन्थे प्रयोजनत्वकथनं युक्तमेवेति ।
Therefore, precisely because the cessation of suffering is of a positive nature, declaring it to be the purpose in this treatise is entirely justified.
टिप्पणी
1.
तद्यथा हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः (छा. ८.३.२) इत्यादिश्रुत्युक्तरीत्या गृहेऽन्तर्निहितो हिरण्यनिक्षेपो विद्यमानोऽपि यावदविद्यमविद्यमानवदविद्ययाप्राप्तवद्भवति ।
According to the manner stated in Śruti: 'Just as those who do not know the terrain, walking over and over above a hidden treasure of gold, do not discover it, even so all these beings, going day after day (in deep sleep) to this realm of Brahman, do not discover it, for they are veiled by untruth' (Chā. 8.3.2), a deposit of gold buried inside one's house, though actually present, remains as if non-existent and unattained as long as one is ignorant of it.
अञ्जनाद्युपायैर्ज्ञातश्चेत् प्राप्तवद्भवति ।
If it is discovered through means such as sight-granting collyrium, it becomes as though attained.
इयमेव नित्यप्राप्तस्य प्राप्तिरित्युच्यते ।
This alone is called 'the attainment of the already eternally attained'.
यथायं दृष्टान्तः, एवमेव अयमात्मा ब्रह्म (बृ. २.५.१९) प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म (ऐ. ३.१) सर्वं खलुमिदं ब्रह्म (छा. ३.१४.१) आत्मैवेदं सर्वम् (छा. ७.२५.२) ब्रह्मैवेदं सर्वम् (बृ. २.५.१) इत्यादिश्रुतिभिः सर्वस्य ब्रह्मत्वोपदेशेन परमानन्दस्वरूपस्य स्वस्य ब्रह्मत्वात् नित्यप्राप्तत्वेऽप्यविद्ययाप्राप्तत्वभ्रमः ।
Just as in this illustration, in the very same way, since by Upaniṣadic declarations such as 'This Self is Brahman' (Bṛ. 2.5.19), 'Consciousness is Brahman' (Ai. 3.1), 'All this is verily Brahman' (Chā. 3.14.1), 'The Self alone is all this' (Chā. 7.25.2), and 'Brahman alone is all this' (Bṛ. 2.5.1), everything is taught to be Brahman, one's own self — whose true nature is supreme bliss — is Brahman, and though eternally attained, there is the delusion of it being unattained due to avidyā.
अखण्डपरमानन्दचिद्रूपब्रह्मैवाहम् इति श्रुतियुक्त्यनुभवैर्जायमानस्वस्वरूपसाक्षात्कार एव नित्यप्राप्तस्य प्राप्तिरिति ।
The direct realization of one's own true nature in the form 'I am indeed Brahman, who is partless consciousness and supreme bliss', arising through Śruti, reasoning, and direct experience, is alone 'the attainment of the eternally attained'.
2.
रज्वां प्रतीयमानसर्पस्य रज्जुरधिष्ठानत्वेन कथ्यते ।
The rope is described as the substratum of the snake appearing in the rope.
मन्दान्धकारे प्रतिभासमानसर्पभ्रमाधिष्ठानस्य प्रकाशसम्बन्धे सति रज्जुरेवेयम् इति निश्चये जाते तत्क्षणादेव सर्पो निवर्तते ।
When the substratum of the snake-illusion seen in dim light comes into contact with light, and the definite cognition 'This is only a rope' arises, the snake ceases from that very instant.
तस्मात्सर्पनिवृत्तितदधिष्ठानरज्जुसाक्षात्कारयोश्चैकक्षणावच्छेदेन जायमानत्वात् सर्पनिवृत्तिरधिष्ठानरज्जुमात्रं भवति ।
Therefore, since the cessation of the snake and the direct perception of the substratum rope occur at the exact same moment, the cessation of the snake is nothing other than the substratum rope itself.
39 · सम्बन्धनिरूपणं
(१) ग्रन्थस्य विषयस्य (प्रमेयस्य) च प्रतिपाद्यप्रतिपादकभावः सम्बन्धः ।
(1) The relation between the treatise and the subject-matter (the truth to be demonstrated) is the relation of the explicated and the explicator (*pratipādya-pratipādaka-bhāva*).
ग्रन्थः प्रतिपादकः, विषयः (जीवब्रह्मैक्यम्) प्रतिपाद्यः ।
The treatise is the explicator; the subject-matter (the identity of *jīva* and *Brahman*) is that which is explicated.
यत् विषयं विविच्य बोधयति तत् प्रतिपादकम्, यत् बोध्यते तत् प्रतिपाद्यम् ।
That which discriminates and explains the subject is the explicator (*pratipādaka*); that which is explained is the explicated (*pratipādya*).
(२) अधिकारिफलयोः प्राप्यप्रापकभावरूपः सम्बन्धः ।
(2) The relation between the qualified aspirant (*adhikārin*) and the fruit (*phala*) is of the nature of the relation between the attained and the attainer (*prāpya-prāpaka-bhāva*).
फलं प्राप्यम्, अधिकारी प्रापकः ।
The fruit is that which is to be attained; the qualified seeker is the attainer.
यद्वस्तु लभ्यते तत् प्राप्यं, यो लब्धा स प्रापकः ।
Whatever entity is obtained is the *prāpya*; whoever is the obtainer is the *prāpaka*.
(३) अधिकारिविचारयोस्तु कर्तृकर्तव्यभावरूपः सम्बन्धः ।
(3) But the relation between the qualified aspirant and inquiry (*vicāra*) is of the form of agent and the action to be performed (*kartṛ-kartavya-bhāva*).
अधिकारी कर्ता, कर्तव्यो विचारः ।
The qualified seeker is the agent; inquiry is that which is to be performed.
यः करोति स कर्ता, यत् क्रियते तत् कर्तव्यम् ।
He who performs is the agent (*kartṛ*); that which is done is the duty (*kartavya*).
(४) ग्रन्थज्ञानयोः जन्यजनकभावः सम्बन्धः ।
(4) Between the treatise and knowledge, the relation is that of produced and producer (*janya-janaka-bhāva*).
विचारद्वारा ज्ञानं प्रति ग्रन्थः जनकः ज्ञानं जन्यम् ।
Through inquiry, the treatise is the producer with respect to knowledge, and knowledge is that which is produced.
यत् उत्पादयति तत् जनकम्, यत् उत्पद्यते तत् जन्यम् ।
That which generates is the producer (*janaka*); that which arises is the produced (*janya*).
एवम् एव सम्बन्धान्तरम् अपि बोध्यम् ।
In the very same manner, the other relations also ought to be understood.
यस्तु साधनसम्पन्नो जिज्ञासुः प्रथमं पठेत् । इमं तरङ्गं सततं मुक्तोऽसौ नात्र संशयः ॥
'Whoever is endowed with the spiritual prerequisites and, being a seeker of truth, regularly studies this first chapter—he is surely liberated; there is no doubt about this.'
टिप्पणी
1.
सम्बन्धरूपानुबन्धकथने प्रयोजनम् — यद्वस्तुनः येन सह सम्बन्धः भवति तस्य तद्विषयेऽपि उपयोगः अस्ति ।
The purpose in stating the prerequisite in the form of relation is this: whatever object has a connection with something, it has utility with respect to that object.
यथा कुलालादीनां घटादीनां सह सम्बन्धोऽस्ति, अतः कुलालादयो घटाद्युत्पत्तिविषये उपयुज्यन्ते ।
Just as potters and others have a relation with pots and the like, therefore potters and others are useful in the production of pots, etc.
यस्य येन सम्बन्धः नास्ति न तस्य तद्विषये उपयोगः अस्ति ।
That which has no connection with something has no utility regarding it.
यथा चक्षुषः वाय्वाकाशाभ्यां सम्बन्धाभावात् तद्विषयीकरणे न उपयोगः ।
Just as the eye, due to lack of connection with air and space, has no capability to perceive them.
एवं ग्रन्थब्रह्मणोः सम्बन्धाभावे ग्रन्थस्य न ब्रह्म विषयो भवेत् ।
Similarly, if there were no relation between the treatise and *Brahman*, *Brahman* would not be the subject-matter of the treatise.
ग्रन्थोऽपि न ब्रह्मप्रतिपादकः स्यात् ।
Nor would the treatise be an explicator of *Brahman*.
तस्मात् परस्परोपकारसिद्ध्यर्थम् अनयोः सम्बन्धः अतद्व्यावृत्त्या बोध्यबोधकभावरूपः कल्प्यते इति ।
Therefore, for the sake of establishing mutual utility, the relation between them is posited through the elimination of what is not That (*atat-vyāvṛtti*) in the form of the relation of the revealed and the revealer (*bodhya-bodhaka-bhāva*).
2.
सम्बन्धान्तरशब्देन श्रवणादेः ज्ञानेन सह, ज्ञानस्य च मोक्षेण सह च साध्यसाधनभावरूपः सम्बन्धः विज्ञेयः ।
By the phrase 'other relations' (*sambandhāntara*), one should understand the relation of means and end (*sādhya-sādhana-bhāva*) between *śravaṇa* etc. and knowledge, as well as between knowledge and *mokṣa*.
